frame.converter: Each sky position onto the midplane of the inclined disc the image layers are baked on (recipe.json), through the image-layer bake's own intersection.

discThickness.basis: The stellar disc's exponential scale height as its scale length over 7.3, the mean flattening Kregel et al. (2002) measured for edge-on discs (the relation the THINGS papers adopt), with S4G's disc scale length (Salo et al. 2015): 368 pc. The same thickness as the image layers' slabs; for young objects it is an upper value. Each row's own height is drawn, not measured.

bulge.basis: Old objects fill the bulge as well as the disc: each is a bulge member with the bulge's share of S4G's fitted light at its sky position (faded out between 3 and 6 kpc as the image layers' is), and then sits at a depth drawn from the bulge's density along its sight line. Membership is drawn, not measured.

meaning: Globular clusters of M81 confirmed by spectroscopy (Nantais & Huchra 2010): one dot per cluster at its catalogue position. Globular clusters belong to the halo and bulge; here they are placed on the disc or, near the centre, in the bulge.

appearance.note: Presentation only: the Milky Way globular clusters' warm orange. Each dot takes its tone and half its color from the photograph under it (packages/bake/cli/prepare-catalogue-points.mts).
